verdict.summary: You can create a General app and connect your own account, or other users in your own Zoom account, in minutes using development credentials. Users outside your Zoom account can install the app only after Zoom's app review passes. That review includes a per-scope Security Review, OWASP-based security testing, domain validation and a test plan, and Zoom publishes no timeline for it.
verdict.hands_on_effort: 30-60 min for your own account; about 1-3 days of preparation (docs, domain validation, technical design, test plan) for a public submission
verdict.approval_wait: Varies. Zoom publishes no fixed review timeline, and failed reviews add remediation rounds.

gates.name: Development credentials (your own account)
gates.unlocks: You can authorize your own Zoom user through your app using the development client ID and secret.
limits: Requires the account owner, an admin, or a user with the 'Zoom for developers' role
Free accounts must first complete a compliance step (Free with Credit Card, or submit developer and entity details)
Access tokens expire after 1 hour and refresh tokens after 90 days

gates.name: Unpublished app used inside your own Zoom account
gates.unlocks: Other users in your own Zoom account can install and authorize the app without Marketplace review.
limits: Only users in your own Zoom account. Zoom has no test-user allowlist for external accounts.
According to a Zoom forum reply, an OAuth app's no-review status cannot be changed to allow external users

Some workspaces require an admin to pre-approve apps before users can add them

gates.name: Published app (public or unlisted) after app review
gates.unlocks: Users in any Zoom account can install and authorize the app.

Every URL domain in the app (privacy policy, terms of use, OAuth redirect, webhook URL, home URL) needs one-time domain validation

gates.time_to_reach: Days to weeks, depending on preparation and review rounds. Zoom publishes no timeline.

steps.title: Confirm you have developer permissions
steps.detail: Sign in to marketplace.zoom.us and check for the Developer link in the lower-left pane. It only appears for the account owner, account admins, or users with the 'Zoom for developers' role. If it is missing, an admin can grant the role under User Management > Roles > Role Settings > Advanced features by ticking View and Edit for 'Zoom for developers'.
gotchas: A community guide reports that a standard user account can't manage OAuth credentials or domain validation

steps.title: Complete the free-account compliance step if needed
steps.detail: If you are on a free Zoom account, either upgrade to Free with Credit Card or submit your developer and entity details through Zoom's form before you build apps.

steps.title: Create a General app
steps.detail: Click the Developer link. On the Created apps page, choose Develop > Build an app and select General app. Pick Server-to-Server OAuth instead only if you need account-level access to a single account rather than per-user authorization.

steps.title: Choose admin-managed or user-managed on Basic Info
steps.detail: On the Basic Info step, choose user-managed if each person authorizes access to only their own data. Choose admin-managed if account admins install the app and it needs data for users across the account. This choice changes which features and scopes are available.

steps.title: Add the Composio callback to the OAuth allow list
steps.detail: Copy the development client ID and client secret from the app's credentials. Enter the redirect URL and add the same URL to the OAuth allow list. The redirect sent during authorization must match an entry in the allow list.

values.label: Redirect URI
values.value: Composio callback URL (see the Composio callout on this page)

gotchas: URLs must use HTTPS and a fully-qualified domain. localhost and unverified ngrok domains are not accepted, and 127.0.0.1 loopback redirects only work for PKCE or native clients.
Development and production credentials are separate. Use the development pair for now.
Confirm the exact callback URL in your Composio auth config. The URLs found during research differed (/api/v1/auth-apps/add vs /api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback).

steps.title: Add minimal scopes with descriptions
steps.detail: Add only the granular scopes your agent actually calls, such as meeting:read:list_meetings or meeting:write:meeting. Write a Scope Description for each one explaining why the app needs it. Drop redundant scopes, such as a view scope that a broader scope already covers.
gotchas: Composio's default set has about 26 scopes. Each one is a separate request to Zoom's Security Review, so trim it.

steps.title: Create a Composio auth config and test the connection
steps.detail: In Composio, create a Zoom auth config that uses your own OAuth app. Enter the development client ID, client secret and the same scopes. Connect your own Zoom account, and confirm the authorization code is exchanged and a meeting list call succeeds.
gotchas: Error 4702 'Invalid client_id' means the client ID is wrong, or you used the production ID before the app was published
Refresh tokens expire after 90 days, after which the user must re-authorize

steps.title: Roll out to users in your own Zoom account
steps.detail: Colleagues in the same Zoom account can authorize the unpublished app without review. If your account requires admin pre-approval of apps, an admin must approve it first.

steps.title: Publish listing pages on your own domain
steps.detail: Draft and host Terms, Privacy Policy, Support and Documentation pages on a fully-qualified domain your company owns. The documentation must cover adding, using and removing the app, and the support page must state hours and a first-response SLA. Prepare 1200x780 px gallery images and optionally one video of up to 40 MB.
gotchas: Pages hosted on Google Drive or Dropbox are rejected

steps.title: Validate every URL domain
steps.detail: In the build flow, complete one-time domain validation for each domain used by the Privacy Policy, Terms of Use, OAuth redirect URL, webhook callback URL and home URL. Validate with a DNS TXT record, an uploaded HTML file or a meta tag, or ask Zoom support for manual approval. Your Composio-hosted redirect domain may need Zoom support's manual approval, because you can't add a DNS record, file or meta tag to Composio's domain.

steps.title: Prepare the security and technical design materials
steps.detail: Complete the required technical design section. Have evidence ready that Zoom may request: SSDLC practices, OWASP-based secure coding, and SAST and/or DAST results. Implement the deauthorization endpoint so that when a user removes the app, you delete their data and revoke the token.

steps.title: Submit for review with a test plan
steps.detail: Put a test plan in the Release Notes field, provide test credentials for each user role, confirm the Marketplace Developer Agreement and submit. For a first submission, configure the app with the production client ID, which reviewers test with. If you request a public (PKCE) client, explain why it is needed.
gotchas: Every resubmission needs a test plan
Later update requests use the development client ID

steps.title: Wait for Zoom's app review
steps.detail: Zoom reviews submission completeness and branding, functionality, usability and compliance, and security, including OWASP Top 10 testing. If the app fails, you get a remediation report and can resubmit once the items are fixed.

steps.title: Switch Composio to the production credentials
steps.detail: Once the app is approved, put the production client ID and secret in your Composio auth config. Then run a test authorization from an account outside your own.

requirements.item: Developer permissions (account owner, admin, or 'Zoom for developers' role)
requirements.detail: The Developer link is hidden without these permissions.
Upgrade to Free with Credit Card, or submit developer and entity details through Zoom's form.

requirements.item: HTTPS redirect on a fully-qualified domain, listed in the OAuth allow list
requirements.detail: localhost, unverified ngrok domains and default Heroku domains are not allowed.
Unjustified or redundant scopes are rejected under Zoom's minimal-access principle.

requirements.item: Domain validation for all app URL domains
requirements.detail: Validate with a DNS TXT record, HTML file, meta tag, or Zoom support's manual approval.

requirements.item: Terms, Privacy, Support and Documentation pages on a domain you own
requirements.detail: Documentation must cover add, use and remove. The support page must give hours and a first-response SLA.

requirements.item: Technical design section and security evidence
requirements.detail: Zoom may request SSDLC, OWASP secure coding, and SAST/DAST evidence.

requirements.item: Test plan and per-role test credentials
requirements.detail: Required on every submission, including resubmissions.
Delete the user's data and revoke the token when the app is removed.

scopes.effect: Each scope goes through Zoom's Security Review and needs a Scope Description. Zoom doesn't publish sensitivity tiers.
Part of Composio's defaults. Request these only if your agent uses transcripts. The delete scope especially needs a clear justification.
Part of Composio's broad default set. Remove any your agent doesn't use, because unused scopes are a rejection reason.
Listed in Zoom's OpenID Connect discovery document. Add them only if you need identity data.

blockers.symptom: There is no Developer link in the Marketplace left pane
blockers.fix: Ask an admin to enable 'Zoom for developers' under User Management > Roles > Role Settings > Advanced features.

blockers.symptom: Error 4702 'Invalid client_id' on the authorize page
blockers.cause: The client ID is wrong, or it doesn't match the app's current state (development vs production)
blockers.fix: Use the development client ID until the app is published, and the production client ID after approval.

blockers.cause: The redirect URL is not in the OAuth allow list, or is not HTTPS on a fully-qualified domain
blockers.fix: Add the exact Composio callback URL to the OAuth allow list.

blockers.symptom: Users outside your Zoom account can't install the app
blockers.cause: Unreviewed apps only work inside the developer's own account
blockers.fix: Submit the app for review and publish it as public or unlisted.

blockers.symptom: A user sees a block message saying an admin must approve the app
blockers.cause: Their workspace requires admin pre-approval of apps
blockers.fix: Ask that workspace's Zoom admin to approve the app.

blockers.symptom: Review rejected over scopes or missing materials
blockers.cause: Redundant or unjustified scopes, a missing test plan, or policy pages on third-party hosts
blockers.fix: Trim the scopes, add Scope Descriptions and a test plan, move pages to your own domain, then resubmit using the remediation report.

composio.note: Start on Composio's managed Zoom app to prototype. This avoids Zoom's app review entirely. Register your own app if you need your own branding or redirect, or control over the app. Your own app works right away for you and users in your Zoom account, but external users need Zoom's full app review. If you go that route, trim Composio's broad default scope set (about 26 scopes) to what your agent actually uses.

evidence.claim: Composio's toolkit record reports managed OAuth for Zoom in OAUTH2 mode, with authorization URL https://zoom.us/oauth/authorize and token URL https://zoom.us/oauth/token.
Apps are created in the Zoom App Marketplace via the Developer link > Develop > Build an app > General app.
Developer permissions (account owner, admin, or the 'Zoom for developers' role) are required, and the Developer link only appears for those users.
Admins grant the 'Zoom for developers' role under User Management > Roles > Role Settings > Advanced features.
Free-account developers must upgrade to Free with Credit Card or submit developer and entity details.
Server-to-Server OAuth is a separate app type for account-level API access.
A community write-up says a standard user account is not enough to manage OAuth credentials, domain validation, and app activation.
Basic Info asks whether the app is admin-managed or user-managed, which changes the available features and scopes.
The build flow generates separate development and production credentials.
The OAuth allow list is a required field, and the redirect must match an entry in it.
All URLs need HTTPS on fully-qualified domains. localhost, unverified ngrok domains, and default Heroku domains are not allowed.
User access tokens expire after one hour and refresh tokens after 90 days.
Public (PKCE) apps must justify why they need a public client ID in production.
Loopback 127.0.0.1 redirects are allowed only for PKCE or native clients. Non-PKCE apps must use HTTPS redirects.
Zoom's OpenID Connect discovery document lists the openid, email, and profile scopes and the PKCE methods plain and S256.
The authorize endpoint returns error 4702 'Invalid client_id' for an invalid client ID.
Each scope is a request to Zoom's Security Review team and needs a Scope Description.
Redundant or unjustified scopes are a rejection reason.
Zoom's docs do not label scopes as sensitive or restricted, and every scope goes through the same Security Review.
Public and unlisted apps go through review, and private and beta apps do not.
The security review includes a technical design section, scope evaluation, and OWASP Top 10 testing.
Zoom may request SSDLC evidence, proof of OWASP-based secure coding, and SAST/DAST results.
Publishing requires one-time domain validation for every URL domain the app uses.
Every submission needs a test plan in Release Notes and test credentials for each user role.
First-time submissions use the production client ID, and update requests use the development client ID.
Policy, support, and documentation URLs must be on company-owned domains, not on Google Drive or Dropbox.
Documentation must cover adding, using, and removing the app, the support page needs hours and an SLA, and gallery images are 1200x780 px.
Failed apps receive a remediation report and can resubmit, and Zoom may remove risky published apps.
Review time varies, and no fixed timeline is published.
External users can install only after review passes, while users in the developer's own account can install without review.
A forum reply says an OAuth app's no-review status can't be changed for external use, though an unpublished app works for users in your own account.
Some workspaces require admin pre-approval of apps, and users see a block message until an admin approves.
The authorization request uses response_type=code with client_id, redirect_uri, and optional PKCE S256.
On app removal, Zoom POSTs to the deauthorization endpoint, and the app must delete the user's data and revoke the token.

open_questions: Zoom publishes no review timeline (for example, in business days). It only says review time varies.
No rate limit or install cap was found for new, unreviewed Zoom OAuth apps.
It's unconfirmed whether any scope triggers review beyond the standard Security Review.
It's unknown whether a free developer account (after the compliance step) can publish an external app, or whether a paid plan or business verification is required.
Confirm the exact Composio callback URL in your auth config. Research found both /api/v1/auth-apps/add and /api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback on backend.composio.dev.
Domain validation for the Composio-hosted redirect domain (backend.composio.dev) probably needs Zoom support's manual approval. This was not confirmed.
